takeaway: TransUNet is a U-shaped network: a CNN turns the CT slice into feature maps, a 12-layer Transformer encodes the deepest map as a token sequence, and the Cascaded Upsampler (CUP) reshapes the tokens and upsamples them back to full resolution, fusing the CNN's high-resolution maps through skip connections, to predict the segmentation mask.

reader_questions.glance: Where is the Transformer in a U-Net, and what goes in and comes out?
reader_questions.detail: Which CNN resolutions are skipped into which decoder step, and what does one CUP step do?

concepts.name: TransBTS row folded into a U lying on its side
concepts.takes: From TransBTS Fig. 1: the left-to-right encoder (input scan, CNN feature maps as shaded 3-D slabs whose height shrinks with resolution), a token sequence entering a Transformer stack drawn as upright slabs with rotated labels (its 'Linear Projection' / 'Transformer Layer' look), and its emphasis rule — the Transformer bottleneck is the only tinted panel, encoder and decoder carry no containers and differ by tint (grey CNN vs blue decoder). The row is folded at the Transformer: the decoder returns underneath, so each skip becomes a short vertical drop between equal resolutions (labelled H/2, H/4, H/8 as on swin-unet-2021-fig1's skip arrows), and the CT slice and the mask stack at the left for direct comparison.
concepts.sketch: Top row: CT slice -> grey slabs H/2, H/4, H/8, H/16 -> orange panel [1x1-patch tokens -> Patch Embedding -> (+) pos. emb. -> Transformer Layer x12]; 'reshape' down into the blue H/16 map; bottom row right-to-left: H/16 -> H/8 -> H/4 -> H/2 -> H -> mask placeholder under the CT. Orange 'Transformer Layer' inset (Eq. 2-3) in the lower right under the Transformer. Brackets name the Hybrid CNN-Transformer Encoder (top) and CUP (bottom).

concepts.name: Upright U (encoder down the left, decoder up the right)
concepts.takes: Swin-Unet's upright U with input and output capping the columns and straight horizontal skips; TransBTS's tinted Transformer panel at the bottom.
concepts.sketch: Prototyped (r0 draft 1): at the 7-pt floor the five stacked resolution levels make the figure ~5 in tall at 4.8 in wide, the U's interior is empty and the two titles collide with the decoder column.

concepts.name: One left-to-right row with skip arcs (TransBTS literal)
concepts.takes: TransBTS Fig. 1 as drawn: input, encoder slabs, central Transformer panel, decoder slabs, output in one row, nested dashed skips arching over the top.
concepts.sketch: 13+ units in one row; at 4.8 in the text falls below the 7-pt floor and the three nested arcs become long parallel lines.

why: The method's message is 'a U-Net whose encoder ends in a Transformer': folding TransBTS's row keeps its reading (scan -> CNN maps -> tokens -> Transformer) and its single tinted Transformer panel, makes each skip a short vertical drop between maps of the same resolution, and puts the input slice directly above the predicted mask. It is the only candidate that fits LNCS's 4.8-in column at the 7-pt floor without a tall or empty layout (upright-u was built and came out ~5 in tall; flat-row cannot reach 7 pt).
highlight: The Transformer bottleneck (1x1-patch tokens, Patch Embedding, + position embedding, Transformer Layer x12) is the only tinted panel in the main line, in the orange accent; one Transformer layer (LN, MSA, residual add, LN, MLP, residual add — Eq. 2-3) is expanded in a matching orange inset directly below it, linked by its name and tint rather than zoom lines; the grey map run is headed 'CNN (ResNet-50)' and the orange panel 'Transformer', so the encoder bracket visibly spans CNN + Transformer; the two proposed parts carry the paper's names on brackets — 'Hybrid CNN-Transformer Encoder' over the top row and 'Cascaded Upsampler (CUP)' under the bottom row — and CUP's maps are drawn in a stronger blue than the muted grey CNN maps.
